title: Inside the D.O.J.’s Investigation of Fauci and Other Virus Scientists
partialText: As Dr. Anthony Fauci has faced public scrutiny from congressional Republicans, the D.O.J. has pursued a quieter and more expansive effort against a wider circle of researchers.

title: In Major Leak Hunt, Pentagon Gives Polygraph Tests to Joint Staff Members
partialText: About 50 people were tested, an unparalleled inquiry that comes in the wake of news reports about the war with Iran and the U.S. military’s diminished stocks of munitions.

title: U.S. Strikes Three Iranian ‘Shadow Network’ Oil Tankers, Military Says
partialText: The U.S. military said it retaliated after Iran launched missiles at two warships. The strikes came days after the two sides exchanged some of their most intense fire in weeks.

title: What the War in Iran Has Cost One Gold Star Family
partialText: First Lt. Tyler James Feehan, who was 25, had been deployed to an air base in Jordan when enemy missiles and drones lit up the sky. He is among the 18 Americans who have died since the war began.

title: Putin Orders Pause in Kyiv Strikes Ahead of Visit by U.S. Envoys
partialText: Steve Witkoff, President Trump’s special envoy, and Jared Kushner, his son-in-law, arrived in Moscow to meet with the Russian leader. They head to Kyiv next, in an effort to revive peace talks.

title: Putin Denies a Draft Is Coming, but Some Russian Men Are Taking No Chances
partialText: As the fear of a possible mobilization becomes a fixture of daily life across Russia, many men are deciding whether to flee, hide or sit tight.

title: What Will Happen to Lindsay Clancy in the Long Term?
partialText: Even as a jury failed to reach a verdict in Lindsay Clancy’s murder trial, her future is unlikely to include freedom, at least for a long time. But Americans have been divided over the goal of her confinement.

title: In Complex Cases Like Lindsay Clancy’s, a Unanimous Verdict Can Be Hard to Reach
partialText: Hung juries are not common, but the murder trial of Lindsay Clancy was emotionally wrenching and uniquely complicated.

title: What Led to Maria Bartiromo’s Downfall at Fox News
partialText: The network this week took Maria Bartiromo off the air, pulling one of the last hosts whose coverage of Dominion Voting Systems drew an expensive defamation lawsuit.

title: In Red States, Law-and-Order Republicans Turn Against Flock Cameras
partialText: The governors of Texas and Florida have taken steps to curtail the use of license-plate readers, even as the police say they help with solving crime.

title: Gallup Polls Show Democrats Outnumber Republicans Ahead of 2026 Midterm Elections
partialText: Data from Gallup shows that Democrats and Democratic-leaning independents have their largest advantage over Republicans since 2008.

title: Missouri Asks Supreme Court to Allow Voting Map Benefiting Republicans
partialText: Missouri’s Supreme Court said a map redrawn to help Republicans could not be used in November and said voters should decide on the new boundaries.

title: Ossoff and Talarico to Share Fund-Raising Event in Hollywood
partialText: The event with the Georgia and Texas Democrats will be hosted by Shonda Rhimes.

title: How Naomi Osaka Became the Fashion Queen of the Tennis Court
partialText: At the U.S. Open she is playing a whole new style game.

title: Harlan Coben’s New Book Is a Tough-Talking Writing Guide
partialText: Even a very successful thriller writer fights self-doubt. His new tough-talking writing guide doubles as a memoir that explains why, and how to beat it.

title: Notre Dame’s Jersey Patch Deal With SoFi Divides Alumni and Fans
partialText: Alumni have varying opinions about the school’s deal with the personal finance company SoFi to advertise on Notre Dame athletic uniforms.

title: The Purest American Culture Lives on at Local Festivals
partialText: Turning hyperlocal traditions into public spectacle is a U.S. pastime.

title: Scenic Route
partialText: The season’s new releases give us a cultural road map, but the most rewarding reading, listening and watching comes from the detours.

title: How Gloria Steinem and Ms. Magazine Transformed the Publishing Industry
partialText: The feminist icon insisted that women were not a niche audience — and proved it in 1971 with the start of an influential publication owned and operated by them.
